description:
Track consulting time per thread; entries are stored under hours/<Kind>/<Thread>.md as JSON in a simple-time-tracker fence.

Subcommands:
  log THREAD DESCRIPTION... [-m MIN] [-r RATE] [-c ISO] [-d DATE] [-t TIME] — append an entry; with no THREAD it runs an INTERACTIVE capture
  list [THREAD] [--since D] [--until D] [--json] — list entries
  report [--thread T] [--since D] [--until D] [--json] — totals by thread and currency
  show ID [--json] — show one entry
  edit ID [--description TEXT] [-m MIN] [-r RATE] [-c ISO] [-d DATE] [-t TIME] — change fields of an entry
  rm ID [-y] — delete an entry

Flags:
  log: -m minutes, default 60; -r hourly rate, 0 means unbillable and hours still count; -c 3-letter ISO currency, defaults to the thread's; -d YYYY-MM-DD, default today; -t HH:MM, default now; --all only affects interactive mode.
  list/report: --since YYYY-MM-DD inclusive; --until YYYY-MM-DD inclusive; --json JSON output.
  edit: same value flags as log, plus --description.
  rm: -y skip confirmation.

THREAD is a thread name, 'Kind/Name', or a wikilink. ID is the 8-hex entry id.

Examples:
  ["log", "Projects/SGB", "Drafted the quarterly report", "-m", "90"]
  ["log", "Projects/SGB", "Client call", "-m", "30", "-r", "0", "-d", "2026-06-01", "-t", "09:30"]
  ["report", "--thread", "Projects/SGB", "--since", "2026-01-01", "--json"]
  ["rm", "a1b2c3d4", "-y"]

Notes:
  `log` with no THREAD is interactive and reads from stdin — never call it that way; always pass THREAD and DESCRIPTION.
  Description is nargs-style: pass each word as its own argv element, or the whole description as one element.
  The thread must exist and must have a currency (from the thread file or -c); logging refuses to write without one.
  Rate and currency are resolved at write time and stored per entry; changing thread defaults never re-prices history.
  `rm` is destructive and prompts unless -y.
  Entry ids share one namespace with `payments`.
